newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, Italy to discuss IRI's debt reduction.
newsitem.headline: EU, Italy to discuss IRI's debt reduction.

text.p: European Competition Commissioner Karel Van Miert will discuss with the Italian government next week progress in reducing the huge debt of state industrial holding company IRI, Commission sources said on Friday.

Under a 1993 agreement between Italy and the Commission, IRI must cut its debt to below 5.0 trillion lire ($3.3 billion) by the end of 1996 with the possibility of an extension if justified by the market situation.
The sources were not aware of any Italian demand to extend the deadline. IRI's debt stood at 25 trillion earlier this year.
The privatisation of IRI's telecommunications group Stet, which is expected in February or March 1997 after successive delays, holds the key to the reduction of its parent's liabilities.

Other outstanding issues between the Commission and Rome include a rescue plan for Banco di Napoli, which involves a capital injection of 2.0 trillion lire by the Italian Treasury, and opening of the country's telecommunications market to competition.

Van Miert was also keen to hear Italy's views on the idea defended by the German Federal Cartel Office of a European competition body that would be independent from the Commission. The plan has so far found little support with the other European capitals and national competition authorities with the apparent exception of Italy's anti-trust body chaired by Giuliano Amato.

Van Miert is due to arrive in Rome on Monday evening. On Tuesday he will meet with Prime Minister Romano Prodi and the ministers in charge of industry, Pierluigi Bersani, post and telecommunications, Antonio Maccanico, and the Treasury Minister Carlo Ciampi, according to the Comission's calendar for next week.
